description:
Finds accounts in the chart of accounts, all of them or those of one `account_type`, each with its parent account. It returns an account's own details, not its transactions. When the company shows account numbers, a `full_name` made of digits can match the account with that number rather than that name.

Returns the v2 request to send, and the webhook payload QuickBooks' answer arrives in (this operation's response_json: its data shape and the status codes to handle).

Possible errors (error.code / error.type; the call result explains each): 1030 unsupported_request, 3150 missing_element, 3210 invalid_value, 3220 not_authorized, 3231 request_not_processed, 3250 feature_not_enabled, 3260 insufficient_permission, 3261 personal_data_access_denied, 3262 payroll_subscription_required, 3264 merchant_services_subscription_required

account_type.description:
The type of QuickBooks account. You can’t create or modify a non-posting account through the SDK, because QuickBooks creates these accounts behind the scenes.

Choose at most one of: `list_id`, or `full_name`, or the set (`account_type`, `active_status`, `currency_filter`, `from_modified_date`, `max_returned`, `name_filter`, `name_range_filter`, `to_modified_date`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

max_returned.description:
Limits the number of objects that a query returns. (To get a count of how many objects could possibly be returned, use the `meta_data` query attribute.)

QuickBooks doesn't page this query: at most this many records come back, in one answer, with no sign of whether more matched. Leave it out for every match, in one answer; one over 4 MB as the Web Connector sends it, about 3 MB of qbXML isn't kept (`error_type` `response_too_large`), so narrow a large one with its filters.
